screening_threshold.scope: sole-pair observed-discrepancy screening threshold: one observed realization of repeatability plus uncontrolled drift, screened and not a bound on either
screening_threshold.role: decision threshold: an effect smaller than this bound is not distinguishable from repeat-plus-drift

timestamps.name: uniform-grid phase error at the top of the analysed band
timestamps.criterion: worst-case phase error of the uniform grid at the top of the analysed band: max_k |t_k - (t_0 + k x uniform_period_s)| x f_max <= 1/16 cycle, one criterion per input, f_max the Nyquist limit of that input's own profile rate
timestamps.justification: a sample the uniform grid places dt away from its recorded time is mis-phased by 2 pi f dt for every resolved component at f, so max|t_k - grid| x f_max is the worst-case phase error over the analysed band; 1/16 of a cycle (pi/8 rad) keeps the worst-placed sample's coherent (zero-lag) weight at cos(pi/8) = 0.924 of its unbiased value, i.e. caps the amplitude bias of the coherent sums and of the PSD cross terms at 7.6%, and keeps every sample inside its own cycle of the fastest resolved component so none can be attributed to a neighbouring cycle. The tolerance is a grid-error tolerance and says nothing about the flow; the four published statistics describe the recorded intervals themselves, while max_grid_residual_s also carries their cumulative departure, which is what a quantized interval accumulates over a record
timestamps.estimator: uniform grid at each record's own mean inter-profile interval, the period its first and last recorded timestamps imply; the residual is measured against that grid, not against a nominal PRF period
timestamps.decision: uniform grid retained: every input's worst-case phase error is below the tolerance at the top of the band it is analysed in, so the recorded timestamps need no resampling and no irregular-time estimator

common_duration.rule: largest integer number of nominal revolutions fitting every burst recording, truncated per file by the recorded timestamps

common_support.rule: the intersection of the decoded depth ranges, used by every summary

depth.native_grid: each level keeps its own decoded gate grid for the distributional metrics, the gradient and the correlation length; nothing is resampled

grid.acf_estimator: biased (divide-by-N) autocovariance of the mean-removed segment

temporal.mixer_setpoint_role: nominal mixer marker only (500 RPM -> 8.33 Hz, one revolution = 0.12 s): no tachometer in these files, so the setpoint is not a phase reference
temporal.rule: every file's full record in non-overlapping segments of the identical profile count on one shared profile period, so the segment duration, lag grid, frequency grid and frequency resolution are identical for all 12 files; each level's ensemble ACF/PSD is summarised in burst-levels.csv

floor.role: sole-pair observed-discrepancy screening threshold: one observed realization of repeatability plus uncontrolled drift, screened and not a bound on either (temporal)

alignment.knot_rule: the longer pulse's native gate depths inside the common support, so the knot spacing is never finer than that participant's own grid
alignment.short_sampling_rule: the shorter pulse's profile is sampled at each knot by its nearest native gate (offset at most half its own pitch); no interpolation

focus_pair.selection: selected by decoded cycle count from the manifest ladder: the plan's question names 18 and 20 cycles, not a filename

definitions.cycles: decoded burst length, re-checked against the manifest burst_length cell
definitions.robust_spread: IQR p75 - p25 across supported gates of the per-gate time means
definitions.rms: root mean square about zero over the common window and support, mm/s; not a sigma
definitions.zero_fraction: samples exactly 0.0 over the common window and support: dropout
definitions.gradient: median and maximum |mean[k+1] - mean[k]| / native pitch, mm/s per mm
definitions.correlation_length: first native lag whose normalized autocovariance < 1/e, mm
definitions.difference: signed short - long per-gate time mean at every common knot, mm/s
definitions.screening_threshold: the committed sole-pair observed-discrepancy screening threshold max_gate_abs_mean_difference_mm_s, read from reference-repeat.provenance.json and pinned to this manifest's hash: the threshold every mean-profile effect is screened against. An effect above or below it is a screening outcome, not proof of a burst effect and not a bound on repeatability or uncontrolled drift
definitions.figure: both panels carry this document's caption and the generating commit
definitions.knee: the largest one-step change of a metric along the ladder, with monotonicity
definitions.temporal_bandwidth: per level, from its full-record ensemble PSD inside 0.5-20 Hz: the spectral centroid and RMS bandwidth, the share of in-band power above 10 Hz, and the e-folding lag of the ensemble autocorrelation
definitions.temporal_floor: the same temporal metrics for the two committed WP1 same-settings recordings, from the curves reference-repeat.provenance.json already records; their difference is the temporal screening threshold for those metrics — one observed realization of repeatability plus uncontrolled drift, not a bound on either
definitions.replicates: no profile and no gate is an independent experimental replicate
definitions.time_view: whole 500-RPM revolutions for every level; the full record for ACF/PSD
definitions.depth_view: each level on its own gate grid inside the common support
definitions.comparability: only the decoded burst length may differ across the ladder

screening_threshold_gate.statement: Effect gate: over the 66 pairs the largest absolute per-knot mean difference is 44.03 mm/s (4 vs 28 cycles) = 2.27 of the WP1 screening_threshold 19.37 mm/s; 21 pairs put a knot above it, 16 of those at the longest bursts, and none covers the support.

focus_18_vs_20.statement: Plan question, 18 versus 20 cycles: the largest absolute per-knot mean difference is 11.75 mm/s at 91.56 mm = 0.607 of the 19.37 mm/s screening_threshold, with 0 of 50 knots above it. Verdict: this evidence cannot support choosing 18 cycles over 20 or the reverse — the difference sits below the screening threshold and no level in the 16-20-cycle region falls above it against any other, so the screening outcome is that nothing is separated. Unidentifiable from this dataset: any burst effect smaller than the screening_threshold, and the pitch x burst interaction, because the two ladders meet only at the reference. What would overturn it: two recordings per cycle count in this region, which would separate the level effect from drift.

focus_window_16_20.statement: 16-20-cycle region: 3 unordered pairs, 0 of them clearing the screening_threshold, so no level differs from another by more than repeat-plus-drift there.

zero_fraction.statement: zero_fraction: largest one-step change +0.01093 across 2-32 cycles, reached at 28 cycles (value 0.02117), net +0.001457; the sequence does not fall monotonically

robust_spread_mm_s.statement: robust_spread_mm_s: largest one-step change +12.88 across 2-32 cycles, reached at 4 cycles (value 34.38), net +8.089; the sequence does not fall monotonically

rms_mm_s.statement: rms_mm_s: largest one-step change -4.843 across 2-32 cycles, reached at 24 cycles (value 35.31), net -0.9909; the sequence does not fall monotonically

correlation_length_mm.statement: correlation_length_mm: largest one-step change +1.85 across 2-32 cycles, reached at 4 cycles (value 12.95), net +1.85; the sequence does not fall monotonically

gradient_max_abs_mm_s_per_mm.statement: gradient_max_abs_mm_s_per_mm: largest one-step change +9.511 across 2-32 cycles, reached at 28 cycles (value 16.14), net +1.215; the sequence does not fall monotonically

psd_hf_share.statement: psd_hf_share: largest one-step change -0.02681 across 2-32 cycles, reached at 6 cycles (value 0.1119), net -0.02061; the sequence does not fall monotonically

acf_e_folding_lag_s.statement: acf_e_folding_lag_s: largest one-step change +0.02239 across 2-32 cycles, reached at 32 cycles (value 0.1119), net +0.02239; the sequence does not fall monotonically

temporal_bandwidth.statement: Temporal bandwidth: the share of in-band power above 10 Hz ranges 0.08851-0.1387 (spread 0.0502) over the 12 levels, the centroid 3.504-4.434 Hz and the RMS bandwidth 4.044-4.725 Hz, against a same-settings repeat floor of 0.02791 in the same share and 0.3759 Hz in the bandwidth: a smaller bandwidth loss is not separable from repeat-plus-drift. The shortest bursts carry the largest share and the longest the smallest, the direction a longer pulse predicts, at a magnitude inside the floor.

spatial_smoothing.statement: Spatial smoothing: the native correlation length of the depth-resolved mean profile is 11.1-14.8 mm over 2-32 cycles (6-8 gate pitches), so the longer pulse is not shown to smooth the profile within this ladder.

limitations: The screening threshold is the only repeat, 19.37 mm/s per gate (max_gate_abs_mean_difference_mm_s): one observed realization of repeatability plus uncontrolled drift, not a bound on either. The levels are separate recordings with no acquisition order, so a smaller effect cannot be separated from drift and a larger one could still be drift or one recording rather than the burst length. No level is replicated.
Temporal metrics are screened against the same-settings WP1 pair through its committed curves (prf/600.BDD vs res/1-8.BDD), and one pair cannot estimate that floor's own spread.

The file carries the velocity-time index only: the 500-RPM setpoint is a marker rather than a phase reference, the ensemble PSD is per gate, and nothing here separates a burst effect from aliased temporal noise or one recording's dropout.

This module owns the burst-length axis only: resolution, PRF, TGC, emitting power and emissions per profile are neither analysed nor decided here, and the pitch x burst interaction is not estimable from this dataset.

Temporal view: full record in 86-profile segments on one shared 0.0223892 s profile period, frequency resolution 0.5194 Hz, Nyquist 22.33 Hz. Temporal floor: prf/600.BDD vs res/1-8.BDD, in-band power above 10 Hz differing by 0.02791.
